
=================================================================
#9 Gwanggaeto, the Great King  (400)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: Part I — The Three Kingdoms / The King for All · place: surabol · tone: fairy-tale legend
Logline: His stele lists sixty-four fortresses. It does not list the nerve it took.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Silla is drowning. An army from across the sea is inside its walls, and its king has one move left.
[1] [CARD Gwanggaeto the Great: Goguryeo’s widest king. The stele ran out of room before he ran out of fortresses.]
[2] [MAP 412: Watch the red run south. One reign did that.]
[3] ── SCENE: The Burning Capital ──
[4] ¶ The Silla king stands on his own wall and counts the sea-raiders’ fires. There are more every night. Below, in the hall, his court is arguing about pride.
[5] A Silla Elder: If we ask the north, they will come. And then they will stay.
[6] The Silla King: And if we don’t ask, the Wa stay. Which guest would you rather feed?
[7] A Silla Elder: Majesty, the letter will have to say… they’ll want a word. A low word.
[8] The Silla King: I know the word. Bring the brush. / I’ll write it myself, so nobody else has to.
[9] ── SCENE: The Plea ──
[10] ¶ His envoy rides north for nine days and kneels in the tent of a Goguryeo king who is twenty-six and has never lost.
[11] Silla’s Envoy: The Wa are inside our walls, Great King. My king writes in his own hand. / “Silla is your servant. Save your servant.”
[12] Gwanggaeto the Great: Servant. He wrote that word himself?
[13] Silla’s Envoy: …In his own hand.
[14] Gwanggaeto the Great: Then they’ll come. Fifty thousand of them. / Tell him one thing more, so he hears it from me first. Servants don’t decide when the master’s horsemen go home.
[15] ¶ The Silla king reads the answer twice. The first half saves his kingdom. The second half he does not read aloud.
[16] ── SCENE: The Horsemen ──
[17] ¶ The horsemen come down out of the north like weather. From his wall the Silla king watches the raiders’ fires go out one by one. Then he watches the red banners come through his own gate, and keep coming.
[18] ¶ A red sun. The three-legged crow rides south on his banners. The stele will list sixty-four fortresses. It will not list the nerve it took.
[19] ¶ They clear the peninsula in a season. Silla had asked. That’s the part everyone forgets. Then the horsemen don’t leave for fifty years.
[20] ¶ Silla’s crown princes go north as hostages. The first one is twelve. Silla’s court takes Goguryeo titles. Silla’s army takes Goguryeo orders. It lasts two generations. Silla does not forget it.
[21] ¶ He goes with a pony and a tutor. At the border he asks how long. Nobody answers him, which is how he finds out.
[22] The Silla Court: They did save us. / So why are they still here?
[23] ¶ His stele, naturally, remembers it more kindly.
[24] ❝QUOTE (Gwanggaeto Stele (廣開土王碑), south face, ll. 3–4 (414 CE); Best, “The Kwanggaeto Stele,” p. 147): The common people were at peace in their work; the country was rich and the people abundant; the five grains ripened in plenty.❞
[25] ¶ Two hundred and forty years later a Silla prince will stand in front of a foreign emperor and ask for an army, and every single person in Surabol will know exactly what that costs, because it has been done to them before.
[26] ¶ **The prince who will beg has a son. Bupmin is fifteen now, and his uncle has one question: which rule will you break first…?**
